clinician.final_diagnosis: superior Foville syndrome due to a pontine hemorrhage
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old previously healthy Senegalese trader presented with abrupt onset (5 days prior to admission) of left body side weakness, acute headaches, and rotatory vertigo. On admission, physical examination revealed paralysis of right oculomotor movements (right gaze palsy), right facial palsy, and left hemiparesis sparing the face, constituting the superior pons type of Foville syndrome. Brain CT scan confirmed spontaneous hemorrhage in the right pontine posterolateral part compressing the fourth ventricle. The patient underwent conservative management with antalgics, anxiolytics, laxatives, and physiotherapy, demonstrated clinical improvement, and was discharged 10 days later.

Spontaneous hemorrhage localized to the right pontine posterolateral region compressing the fourth ventricle
Conservative treatment with clinical improvement and discharge at 10 days
